turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Morning. Obs are done. Blood pressure's 148 over 86, heart rate 76. He wouldn't stand for a weight.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): Ta. Err, what did this morning's bloods show?
[SEG0003] person_1 (NURSE): Creatinine's 168, eGFR's 38. He wasn't fasting. I'll hang about, it's quiet. My little one's got a cold so I swapped onto an early.
[SEG0004] person_3 (PATIENT): Can we just get on with it. I'm only here for the kidney check and I'm bloody tired.
[SEG0005] person_2 (DOCTOR): Yep. Type 2 diabetes and the kidney disease, that's the review. The tiredness —
[SEG0006] person_3 (PATIENT): Yeah I know. Tired for months. I nod off after lunch. And the knee, that's what's actually doing my head in.
[SEG0007] person_2 (DOCTOR): How long's the knee been?
[SEG0008] person_3 (PATIENT): Few weeks. I don't really...
[SEG0009] person_4 (CAREGIVER): Longer than that. Two months, easy, he was limping before Easter. I've been staying at his place since then, so I see it.
[SEG0010] person_3 (PATIENT): Was I? Anyway it aches. Worse at night.
[SEG0011] person_2 (DOCTOR): You getting something from the chemist for it?
[SEG0012] person_3 (PATIENT): Just the shop ibuprofin. Two tablets when it's bad. Not every day.
[SEG0013] person_2 (DOCTOR): What strength are they?
[SEG0014] person_3 (PATIENT): Umm the box says...

[SEG0015] person_4 (CAREGIVER): 200 each. He takes two, so 400, and some days he does that again at night. My sister's mad on biotin for her nails, keeps posting me bottles, but that's her thing not his.
[SEG0016] person_2 (DOCTOR): Right, so some days that's 400 twice, 800 all up. Any swelling in the ankles?
[SEG0017] person_3 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0018] person_2 (DOCTOR): Chest pain?
[SEG0019] person_4 (CAREGIVER): Oh, the parking ticket, it —
[SEG0020] person_3 (PATIENT): No. No chest pain. I'm not puffed. Wee's fine too, no burning, before you go there.
[SEG0021] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any blood in the urine?
[SEG0022] person_3 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0023] person_2 (DOCTOR): Allergies to any medicines?
[SEG0024] person_3 (PATIENT): No. Nothing.
[SEG0025] person_4 (CAREGIVER): Sorry. He didn't eat. I took my own perindopril at six, not his, mine, and then we were running late.
[SEG0026] person_3 (PATIENT): Don't start on breakfast. I'm not hungry mornings.
[SEG0027] person_2 (DOCTOR): The ramipril, still 5 milligrams every morning?
[SEG0028] person_3 (PATIENT): Yeah. The rampril. I don't miss that one.
[SEG0029] person_2 (DOCTOR): And metformin?
[SEG0030] person_3 (PATIENT): 500 twice a day. With food, when there is food.
[SEG0031] person_4 (CAREGIVER): The evening one gets skipped. Three nights a week, easy.
[SEG0032] person_3 (PATIENT): Not three. One or two. I'm not counting them.

[SEG0033] person_2 (DOCTOR): Alright, we'll call the metformin 500 milligrams twice a day and note we're not sure every dose goes in. Thinking it through, ibuprofen clamps the artery going into the kidney, the ramipril opens the one leaving, the filter pressure drops and the creatinine climbs. That's your 168 and the eGFR of 38, I reckon, not the diabetes suddenly chewing more filter. Diabetes does dull the nerves in the feet over the years, but that's a separate story and your feet aren't the problem today.
[SEG0034] person_3 (PATIENT): So the rampril stays.
[SEG0035] person_2 (DOCTOR): Stays. Continue ramipril 5 milligrams each morning. Ibuprofen stops today, full stop. I'll put paracetamol on a script, one gram up to four times a day, for the knee.
[SEG0036] person_3 (PATIENT): Panadol. Fine.
[SEG0037] person_2 (DOCTOR): Nurse, can you take repeat bloods Thursday morning, creatinine and eGFR again. Ramipril after the test, not before.
[SEG0038] person_1 (NURSE): Thursday morning, yep. I'll book him at 8. No fasting needed.
[SEG0039] person_2 (DOCTOR): If those numbers come back borderline we'll add a urine albumin creatinine ratio. Not ordering that today.
[SEG0040] person_3 (PATIENT): More tests. Great.
[SEG0041] person_2 (DOCTOR): And if the knee hasn't settled in a fortnight, then a knee x-ray. Only if it hasn't.
[SEG0042] person_4 (CAREGIVER): He won't ice it. I've said.
[SEG0043] person_2 (DOCTOR): Ice it, and keep the knee moving gently, don't rest it the whole time. Still no nurofen.
[SEG0044] person_3 (PATIENT): Yeah yeah.
[SEG0045] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'll see you back here in a fortnight with the Thursday results. That's booked.
[SEG0046] person_3 (PATIENT): Fortnight. If I'm still standing.
[SEG0047] person_4 (CAREGIVER): I'll get him here.
[SEG0048] person_2 (DOCTOR): Knee's not red and it's not hot. The bend's a bit short of full. That's enough for today.
[SEG0049] person_1 (NURSE): I'll put Thursday at 8 in the book on the way out.

spec.situation: Older diabetic with kidney disease on review; creatinine and eGFR read aloud; takes ibuprofen from a shop against advice; ramipril continued, painkiller advice changed.

traps.happens: The doctor (or nurse) explains a mechanism or a diagnosis in the patient's body ('the voice box is irritated by reflux', 'diabetes dulls the nerves in the feet', 'the swelling is your body fighting infection'). A nurse or caregiver also mentions a fact about THEIR OWN life (their sister, their child, their own illness).
traps.label_rule: Explanations by the doctor are NEVER symptoms, history or social history of the patient; they may only appear as clinical_assessment or counselling if the doctor stated them as such. A nurse's or caregiver's own life facts are not recorded as the patient's. Each symptom's reported_by is the person who really described it.

traps.happens: In the plan the doctor books some tests or visits for a definite time ('the nurse takes bloods Thursday morning', 'I'll see you in two weeks') and makes others conditional ('if those are borderline we do the third test', 'if it does not settle, a scan').
traps.label_rule: Booked or arranged = status planned. Only the hedged ones are conditional. Never mark a booked test conditional or 'if needed'. Instructions for the booked test (fasting, time, medicine timing) belong to that test's action, not a separate invented plan item.

features: third_party_medicine: someone mentions a medicine or condition that belongs to a relative or friend (the sister's biotin, the husband's metformin). It must not appear as the patient's own; a relative's illness can only be family history if said as such.
interruptions_trailing_off: people interrupt each other, trail off, or the answer comes two turns after the question.

omissions.text: Weight was not obtained because the patient would not stand for it.
Current symptom detail for tiredness: the patient nods off after lunch.
Negative finding asked and answered: the patient denied being short of breath ('I'm not puffed').
Negative urinary symptom asked/answered by patient: urine is 'fine' with no burning, i.e. no dysuria.
Current investigation detail missing: creatinine was 168 and eGFR was 38 on this morning's bloods; the patient was not fasting.
Plan detail missing: follow-up in a fortnight is already booked, and it is specifically to review the Thursday results.
